summary: The chosen u' and the given u differ by an element of K(g), so their simple-root sums differ by an element of gR, on which ψ(g⁻¹·) is 1.

steps.claim: Unfold phase at y (the condition holds with u); let k be the chosen element of 𝖴 with k⁻¹y ∈ K(g).
steps.lean: rw [phase, dite_eq_left ⟨u, hu, e⟩]; generalize_proofs k; have := k.choose_spec

steps.claim: ψ(g⁻¹σ(k)) = ψ(g⁻¹σ(u)): k⁻¹u ∈ K(g) ∩ 𝖴 so σ(u) − σ(k) = σ(k⁻¹u) ∈ gR and ψ is trivial on R (self-duality).
steps.lean:
rw [← mul_one (P.ψ _), ← (self_dual _).2 (inv_mul_simpleRootSum_mem (div_mem this.2 e)) 1
    (one_mem _), one_mul, ← P.ψ.map_add_eq_mul, ← mul_add, ← simpleRootSum_mul] <;> simp [*]
